text: Assessing and optimising this asset — starting with measured identification, then diagnosis and corrective actions.
Identification is in: washer at 1383 rpm (23.05 Hz, p_map=1.0), but the scale is uncalibrated and 1× sits above the 15 Hz video Nyquist. Reporting findings before optimising.

title: Speed identified with high posterior confidence — no display check
summary: Speed posterior MAP 1382.9 rpm (23.05 Hz), CI68 1382.9–1385.0 rpm, p_map=1.0, 17/18 peaks explained, source audio (blade pass) refined by kinematic posterior, prior scale-invariant. No display_rpm was read (null), so there is no independent display check/reportable display error. Note 23.05 Hz is above the video Nyquist 15.0 Hz (fps 30, near_nyquist_warning=true), so the video channel alone cannot resolve 1× — speed rests on audio.

title: Amplitudes uncalibrated — no ISO 20816 zone reportable
summary: scale_calibrated=false and overall iso_zone=null, so ISO zones and absolute mm/s severity are NOT reported. Raw channel values 230.5 mm/s (s1 control panel), 105.2 mm/s (s2 front panel), 104.3 mm/s (s3 top edge) are physically implausible/relative only. Valid conclusion is ratio only: control panel moves ~2.2× front/top panels (230.5/105.2 and /104.3). Frequencies, orders, phase and ratios remain usable.

title: Mechanical looseness — leading evaluable fault, moderate probability
summary: Looseness P=0.248 (prior 0.08, evaluable=true) — highest evaluable fault. Evidence: 9 shaft harmonics 1–10× above 10 dB at +9.6 dB (many harmonics → looseness rule), partly offset by half-order lines at −3.8 dB. P<0.5, so this is a lead for inspection, not a confirmed diagnosis. Control-panel relative amplitude ~2.2× other panels is consistent with a panel/mount check, but does not localise a loose joint by itself.

title: Structural modes identified; resonance at operating speed unlikely
summary: FDD structural modes: 2.29 Hz ζ=5.24% sv_ratio 8.3, 3.34 Hz ζ=3.67% sv_ratio 11.0, 4.45 Hz ζ=2.91% sv_ratio 32.3, 6.09 Hz ζ=2.33% sv_ratio 42.7 (phases to −149°/−178° on top edge at 2–3 Hz = panel flexure shapes); residual structural peak 2.34±0.23 Hz. Campbell criticals=[], resonance P=0.030 (prior 0.12) with −6.5 dB for 'critical speed inside swept range'=0. Operating 1382.9 rpm is far above the 2.3 Hz criticals (~70 rpm 2×, ~141 rpm 1× per optimiser), so no order line crosses a natural frequency in steady operation — only transient pass-through on ramp-up/down.

title: Imbalance, misalignment, bearing and cavitation not evaluable — better capture needed
summary: Imbalance P=0.15 (=prior), misalignment 0.10, flow 0.10, cavitation 0.08, bearing 0.08, rotor_bar 0.05 all evaluable=false with no evidence — these are priors, not findings, and must not be concluded or ruled out. Orders 1×/2×/3× are all 0.0 mm/s and 1×=23.05 Hz exceeds video Nyquist 15.0 Hz. Cavitation index 0.349 (HF energy 7.7%, kurtosis 0.24) with audio cavitation_like=false is not a cavitation diagnosis for a washer in any case. Needed capture: tach-referenced accelerometer or >50 fps (preferably ≥60 fps) video so 1×/2× amplitude and cross-coupling phase (~180° rule for misalignment) are resolved, plus calibrated scale reference for absolute severity.

text: Optimiser returned a feasible lower setpoint. Sending it for human approval — note it changes wash/spin duty, so this is a proposal, not an automatic change.

rationale: Digital twin proposes 1107.2 rpm vs current 1382.9 rpm (feasible band 1107.2–1382.9 rpm), meeting the 80% minimum-duty constraint exactly, expected −19.6% vibration and −48.7% energy (0.100→0.051 kW, cubic affinity trend). It holds ≥10% resonance margin from the 2.3 Hz criticals (~141 rpm 1×, ~70 rpm 2×), with P(resonance)=0% current and proposed (threshold 5%) and skip bands 63.3–77.3 / 126.6–154.7 rpm far below the setpoint. NPSH is not applicable to this washer (no pump suction duty identified); remaining caveat is process acceptance — 20% lower drum speed may reduce spin extraction/wash performance, and absolute vibration benefit is relative-only because scale_calibrated=false. Human approval required.

result.markdown:
# WO-261104-5E044 · Washer W-1

**Priority:** P4 (next planned outage)  
**Failure mode:** VIB – Vibration (ISO 14224)  
**Suspected cause:** Mechanical looseness (foundation, hold-down, bearing fit) (posterior 0.25)  
**Raised by:** muse-wonder-1.0 · 2026-11-04 14:15

Looseness is the leading evaluable fault at P=0.248 (9 shaft harmonics 1–10× above 10 dB, +9.6 dB), with the control panel showing ~2.2× the relative motion of the front/top panels. Inspect and torque control-panel and cabinet fasteners, check levelling feet/floor contact, suspension/damper mounts and drum fixings; do not balance — imbalance is non-evaluable (P=0.15, prior only). Re-capture afterwards with tach reference to confirm harmonics reduce.

## Evidence
- shaft harmonics 1-10× above 10 dB = 9 (+9.6 dB)
- half-order lines (dB) = 4.5 (-3.8 dB)
- Amplitudes uncalibrated: severity from frequencies and ratios
- Running speed 1383 rpm (audio (blade pass) · refined by kinematic posterior)

## Safety
- Lock out / tag out (LOTO) the drive and isolate process energy
- Guards back on before restart; no loose clothing near rotating parts

## Tasks
1. Inspect hold-down bolts and grout; check for cracked baseplate welds.
2. Torque bolts to specification in sequence.
3. Re-measure: shaft harmonic series 1-10x reduced; no half-order lines.

**Estimated time:** 1.5 h

## Verification
Re-measure with Argonaut after the work; acceptance: fault posterior < 0.2 and ISO zone A/B (or unchanged frequencies/ratios if uncalibrated).

title: Impact of 1107 rpm setpoint: −48.7% power at the duty point
rationale: Digital twin: 0.100 kW at 1382.9 rpm → 0.051 kW at 1107.2 rpm, Δ=0.049 kW (−48.7%), expected vibration −19.6% (relative scale only, scale_calibrated=false). Annual kWh/cost/CO₂ cannot be stated from the evidence — no annual duty hours, tariff or grid factor were provided; on a transparent basis the saving is 48.7 kWh per 1,000 operating hours at that duty point, and a domestic washer's intermittent duty will make the true annual figure far smaller. # WO-261104-1AC66 · Washer W-1

**Priority:** P4 (next planned outage)  
**Failure mode:** VIB – Vibration (ISO 14224)  
**Suspected cause:** Forcing frequency coincident with a structural natural frequency (posterior 0.03)  
**Raised by:** muse-wonder-1.0 · 2026-11-04 14:15

No connected drive (action a40a50 needs_drive), so apply as a controller step, not an automatic programming: if the washer controller supports skip/dwell-avoid, avoid sustained operation at 63–77 rpm and 127–155 rpm during ramp through the 2.34 Hz structural criticals; otherwise ensure ramp passes promptly without dwell. Steady setpoints 1107–1383 rpm are unaffected. Resonance P=0.030 only — precautionary transient measure.

## Evidence
- critical speed inside the swept range = 0 (-6.5 dB)
- Amplitudes uncalibrated: severity from frequencies and ratios
- Running speed 1383 rpm (audio (blade pass) · refined by kinematic posterior)

## Safety
- Lock out / tag out (LOTO) the drive and isolate process energy
- Guards back on before restart; no loose clothing near rotating parts

## Tasks
1. Program VFD skip frequencies over the resonance bands (Argonaut can do this).
2. If the duty needs that speed: detune the structure. To move fn above the forcing by 15 %, stiffness must rise by the factor computed below (mass unchanged). Here: fn = 2.34 Hz, 1x = 23.05 Hz -> stiffness x127.89 (fn ∝ √k).
3. Re-run a coast-down; confirm the Campbell crossing has moved out of the operating range.

## Parts
- Bracing / stiffener per detuning calculation

**Estimated time:** 1.0 h

## Verification
Re-measure with Argonaut after the work; acceptance: fault posterior < 0.2 and ISO zone A/B (or unchanged frequencies/ratios if uncalibrated).

text:
## Assessment — Washer W‑1

**Running speed:** 1382.9 rpm (23.05 Hz), speed posterior MAP probability `p_map = 1.0`, CI68 1382.9–1385.0 rpm, 17/18 peaks explained. Source: audio (blade pass), refined by kinematic posterior. No display RPM was read, so no independent display-error check is available.

**Evidence limitations**
- `scale_calibrated = false`, overall ISO zone `null`. Therefore **no ISO 20816 severity zone or absolute mm/s severity is reported**. Channel values are relative only: control panel 230.5 (relative mm/s), front panel 105.2, top edge 104.3 — i.e. control panel moves ≈2.2× the other panels.
- Video Nyquist is 15.0 Hz (30 fps) with a near-Nyquist warning, while 1× is 23.05 Hz. The video channel cannot resolve 1×/2×; speed rests on audio.
- Orders 1×/2×/3× are all 0.0 mm/s in the identification.

**Leading fault — mechanical looseness (unconfirmed)**
- Looseness is the leading *evaluable* fault: P = 0.248 (prior 0.08).
- Supporting evidence: 9 shaft harmonics 1–10× above 10 dB (+9.6 dB). Half-order evidence is negative (−3.8 dB).
- This is an inspection lead (P < 0.5), not a confirmed diagnosis.

**Structural modes / resonance**
- FDD structural modes at 2.29 Hz (ζ=5.24%), 3.34 Hz (ζ=3.67%), 4.45 Hz (ζ=2.91%) and 6.09 Hz (ζ=2.33%); residual peak 2.34 ± 0.23 Hz.
- Campbell criticals: none in operation. Resonance P = 0.030. Steady running at 1382.9 rpm is well away from the 2.3 Hz criticals (~141 rpm at 1×, ~70 rpm at 2×); only ramp-through is relevant.

**Not evaluable — better capture required**
Imbalance (P=0.15), misalignment (0.10), cavitation (0.08) and bearing defect (0.08) are `evaluable=false` — these are priors, not findings, and are neither confirmed nor excluded. Needed: a tach-referenced accelerometer or ≥60 fps capture with a calibrated scale reference, so 1×/2× amplitudes and cross-coupling phase can be resolved.

## Optimisation — proposal p81881, awaiting human approval

Digital twin proposes **1107.2 rpm** vs current 1382.9 rpm (feasible band 1107.2–1382.9 rpm):
- Duty constraint met exactly at 80% of current; ≥10% resonance margin (P(resonance) = 0% current and proposed, threshold 5%).
- Expected: −19.6% vibration, −48.7% energy (0.100 → 0.051 kW).
- These are twin-relative figures; absolute vibration benefit cannot be verified until the scale is calibrated. Process caveat: 20% lower drum speed may reduce spin extraction. NPSH is not applicable to this asset. Exclusion bands: 63.3–77.3 rpm and 126.6–154.7 rpm.

## Actions queued
- **WO‑261104‑5E044 (P4, next planned outage)** — looseness: torque control-panel/cabinet fasteners, check levelling feet/floor contact, suspension/damper mounts and drum fixings; then re-capture with tach reference.
- **WO‑261104‑1AC66 (P4)** — skip bands could not be programmed (`needs_drive`: no connected drive), so they are a controller step: avoid dwell at 63–77 / 127–155 rpm during ramp. Note: disregard the auto-generated “stiffness ×127.9” task in that order — resonance P=0.030, pass-through is sufficient.
- **No balancing** — imbalance is non-evaluable at P=0.15 (< 0.5 threshold).
- **Impact (twin accounting, proposal only):** 0.049 kW saved → 292 kWh/yr, ≈$35.04/yr, 0.131 t CO₂/yr, on the stated assumptions of 6000 h/yr, $0.12/kWh and 0.45 kg CO₂/kWh. Equivalent rate: 48.7 kWh saved per 1,000 operating hours — rescale to actual washer duty before claiming annual savings.
- **Follow-up:** re-measurement scheduled, due 2027‑02‑02 (90 days), with tach-referenced calibrated capture.
